summary: Thursday (titles, covers, first frame) for the geography channel: added 3 what-if topics with millions-view references (Pangaea 12M, Mediterranean 6.9M, Bering bridge 2.9M) and one small cover proposal.
why: The feed had 3 open what_if_world topics against 11 why_shaped, and the planner alternates formats. 96% of our views come from the Shorts feed, so the title barely matters for discovery; covers that say 'it' instead of the place are a cheap fix for search and channel-page taps.

findings.title: 96% of views come from the Shorts feed, 2.8% from search
findings.detail: Cover click-through 0-7.1% on 22-363 impressions; the first frame is what decides, and ours already shows the place, flag and source.

findings.title: 5 of our last 8 covers say 'it' or 'here' instead of the place
findings.detail: thumbnail.tag holds the name but Thumbnail.tsx only draws it inside a figure card; proposal geo-cover-names-the-place.

findings.title: What If Pangea Came Back? 12M views on a 392K channel
findings.detail: The strongest what-if demand in the niche; added as a high-priority topic.

findings.title: What If Mediterranean Sea Becomes Lake?? 6.9M on 92.1K subs (75x)
findings.detail: It really happened 5.96 million years ago; added with six sourced figures.

findings.title: Emoji, caps and hashtags in breakout titles: no clear effect
findings.detail: Median views with vs without differ little (217K vs 174K emoji, 168K vs 215K hashtags); no title test queued.

changes.title: 3 topics added to the feed
changes.detail: Pangaea, Mediterranean dried up, Bering Strait bridge (all what_if_world).

changes.title: Proposal geo-cover-names-the-place
changes.detail: Draw the place name on scene covers whose words don't name it, behind a flag.
